title: Comparative Timeline: Route & Model Performance Dashboard (Prototype + Charts)
creator: Amira Patel
description:
Purpose: Design and validate a comparative timeline view that surfaces per-model and per-route performance metrics (latency P50/P95/P99, throughput requests/sec, token consumption, error rate) across selectable time windows and aligned to rollout events. The goal is a single-pane view where SREs, platform engineers, and product owners can quickly compare model variants and routes, correlate spikes to rollouts or config changes, and drill into token-level cost drivers.

Scope:
- High-fidelity prototype for timeline canvas + side-by-side model comparison panel.
- Chart specification for each metric (recommended chart type, aggregation windows, axis behavior, thresholds, tooltip content).
- Interaction spec: hover, brush-to-zoom, aligned multi-series cursor, event markers for rollouts/releases, and quick linkouts to request-level traces.
- Accessibility and color palette guidance for multi-series charts (colorblind-safe, high contrast).

Non-goals: Full console implementation, backend telemetry schema changes, native alerting UI (these are handled by ENG/PM tickets).

Deliverables:
1) Figma prototype with three main states: overview (90d), focused day (24h), and comparison snapshot for two selected models/routes.
2) Chart spec doc with encoding rules (line vs area vs bar), recommended aggregation (1m/5m/1h depending on range), smoothing policy, and sampling rules for streaming data.
3) Interaction flow and microcopy for annotations and event markers (e.g., "canary rollout", "model fallback").
4) Usability test script and results summary (3 sessions internal + 2 customer-facing).

Design decisions & trade-offs:
- Use aligned multi-series line charts rather than stacked area to avoid obscuring low-volume models. Trade-off: requires careful color and label treatment; mitigated by persistent side labels and on-hover emphasis.
- Default aggregation: auto-select 5m buckets for windows >24h, 1m for <=24h. This balances noise vs CPU for rendering.
- Token metrics displayed in separate pane (tokens/sec and cost estimate) to avoid conflating with latency; link token spikes to top routes in side panel.

Acceptance criteria:
- Prototype demonstrates coherent drill path from timeline -> per-route breakdown -> request sampler.
- Chart spec includes encoding for at least latency P50/P95/P99, throughput, tokens, errors, and ability to overlay rollout markers.
- Visual palette passes WCAG AA for text and chart element contrast.
- Usability test median task success >= 80% for identifying root cause of a latency spike.

Implementation notes for engineers:
- Provide sample telemetry payload examples (time-series keys, expected tag names like route, model_id, rollout_id). See Confluence attachment.
- Request a small backend change: rollout_event objects should include standardized start/end timestamps and optional "impact_label" to surface in annotations. Logged as ENG-4321.

Next steps:
- Resolve design feedback from Eng review (11/14) and update Figma of axis labels and legend interactions.
- Run lightweight usability sessions (internal) and incorporate notes.
- Hand-off package to engineering (charts spec + tokens example + prototype) by 2025-11-21.
acceptance_criteria: Prototype with overview and focused states exists in Figma and is linked in attachments
Chart spec contains encoding rules for latency (P50/P95/P99), throughput, tokens, and errors
Event markers for rollouts can be applied and show metadata on hover
Color palette is colorblind-safe and meets WCAG AA contrast for key elements
Usability test median task success >= 80% for root-cause identification
